params.p: [1:tc Particular] Box emitter spreads a small, countable snowfall across the frame width
[1:tc Particular] Emitter is wider than the comp so flakes enter across the entire top edge
[1:tc Particular] Low emission rate keeps the flake population clearly countable
[1:tc Particular] Long enough life for flakes to remain visible while falling slowly
[1:tc Particular] No launch velocity keeps the movement gentle rather than stormy
[1:tc Particular] Uniform emission avoids a directional spray pattern
[1:tc Particular] Positive gravity provides the primary slow downward fall
[1:tc Particular] Air resistance makes wind influence smooth and prevents fast acceleration
[1:tc Particular] Negative X wind produces a consistent leftward drift
[1:tc Particular] No vertical wind so gravity remains the readable downward motion
[1:tc Particular] Glow Sphere particle type gives every flake a naturally soft edge
[1:tc Particular] Small flake size preserves a sparse snow-scale appearance
[1:tc Particular] High size variation makes individual flakes feel organic
[1:tc Particular] Moderate opacity keeps teal flakes visible but delicate
[1:tc Particular] Subtle opacity variation avoids identical-looking particles
[1:tc Particular] Set Color to At Birth before assigning the teal flake color
[1:tc Particular] Cool teal tint for the snowflakes
[1:tc Particular] Normal compositing keeps snow soft and opaque rather than neon-additive
[1:tc Particular] Small particle glow radius feathers each flake
[1:tc Particular] Restrained glow opacity keeps flakes soft without hazing the frame
[1:tc Particular] Keeps the wide emitter just above frame while giving the snowfall a nearly imperceptible natural lateral variation (expr)
[2:PEDG] Very gentle bloom softens only the visible flake highlights
[2:PEDG] Compact bloom radius preserves separated, countable flakes
[2:PEDG] Threshold limits bloom to bright teal flakes and leaves the dark background clean
[2:PEDG] Soft threshold transition avoids harsh halo edges
